responseText: {"title":"Ground, Light, Surround","question":"When does the surrounding space become part of the subject?","introduction":"Sixteen works move between open landscape and enclosed figure, between cast light and dense mark. None of them lets the background stay neutral. A building dissolves into its field; a face is pressed by radiance from outside; a river valley holds as much weight as any portrait. This exhibition traces the ways a surrounding space can redirect, contain, or charge what sits inside it.","closing":"Each work leaves the boundary between subject and surround unsettled. Whether that pressure comes from light, ground, or enclosure remains an open question in every room.","chapters":[{"title":"Grounds That Will Not Stay Still","introduction":"Three works where the space beneath and around a form refuses to recede — the ground is as active as anything placed on it.","stops":[{"slot":"W023","whyHere":"A gabled building holds its shape through repeated misaligned outlines while neon verticals and a pale band below compete equally for attention with the structure itself.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W150","whyHere":"Golden hillsides and a blue channel carry the same restless scribble energy as the building's surroundings, but here no single form anchors the field — the landscape is the subject.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where the building in the previous work was framed by charged marks, here those marks have spread across the entire surface with no structure left to contain them."},{"slot":"W290","whyHere":"Turquoise sweeps and maroon hollows press against each other across three horizontal zones; white looping lines hold the lower mass together without resolving it into any readable form.","transitionFromPrevious":"The previous work's golden hillside and blue channel reappear here in broader, more turbulent form — the same palette pushed toward dissolution rather than legibility."}]},{"title":"Canopy, Cloud, Open Air","introduction":"Three works where marks accumulate into something sky-like or foliage-like, and the question of inside versus outside becomes genuinely uncertain.","stops":[{"slot":"W072","whyHere":"Yellow clusters spread above dark upright forms in an arrangement that can suggest trees, with translucent areas softening the boundary between support and canopy.","transitionFromPrevious":"After the pressured horizontal zones of the previous work, the vertical movement here — dark forms rising into spreading yellow — introduces a different kind of spatial layering."},{"slot":"W064","whyHere":"Horizontal white lines rule across vertical color, holding yellow and orange masses above while blue strokes fall below; the two movements meet without resolving.","transitionFromPrevious":"The canopy-like yellow of the previous work reappears, but now white ruled lines impose a grid that the color refuses to respect, creating a different tension between order and spread."},{"slot":"W046","whyHere":"A dark figure sits amid billowing white loops on a blue-lavender ground while a warm solar disc pulls from upper left — the surrounding air is as weighted as the figure within it.","transitionFromPrevious":"The soft yellow masses of the previous work condense here into a single disc, and the open field below the figure carries the same loose, cloud-like quality the earlier work spread across its whole surface."}]},{"title":"Faces Under Pressure","introduction":"Four works where a face or head is surrounded by forces — light, color field, enclosing marks — that the face cannot fully absorb or deflect.","stops":[{"slot":"W098","whyHere":"Yellow floods the upper field while olive pools below, splitting the face across two tones; a faint blue rectangle floats over the center like a second, cooler layer pressing in.","transitionFromPrevious":"The solar disc from the previous work has expanded here into an entire yellow field that the face must occupy rather than observe."},{"slot":"W133","whyHere":"Dense black hatching buries the face's surface while a yellow loop arcs outside the form, pulling attention around the figure rather than into it.","transitionFromPrevious":"Where the previous face was split by a color field, this one is buried under hatching — the surrounding space is quieter but the surface pressure has moved inward."},{"slot":"W056","whyHere":"A broad fan of pale light pushes from the left across gold and ochre bands while a heavy black arc holds the right edge; the face-like reading of the composition is held in tension between openness and weight.","transitionFromPrevious":"The yellow loop outside the previous figure becomes here a full light source pushing across the frame, and the dark mass that resisted it shifts from hatching to a single heavy arc."},{"slot":"W153","whyHere":"A gold-olive mass fills the frame, its surface built from crossing scribble lines; a diagonal light beam cuts across the upper left while a dark cavity below reads as tense against the calm background spirals.","transitionFromPrevious":"The light fan of the previous work narrows here into a single diagonal beam, and the mass it strikes is denser and more resistant than the open bands it crossed before."}]},{"title":"Light as Enclosure","introduction":"Four works where light does not simply illuminate but surrounds, seals, or structures the forms inside it.","stops":[{"slot":"W196","whyHere":"A form sits sealed inside a dome while gold rays push outward from behind it; the enclosure reads as both lit from within and pressed upon from without, the floating pale circles softening neither reading.","transitionFromPrevious":"The diagonal beam of the previous work has expanded here into a full radial burst, and the form it surrounds is now literally enclosed rather than merely struck."},{"slot":"W183","whyHere":"The image divides between a dark layered left mass and a blazing yellow-gold right field where two white discs burn; red blocks at the bottom feel heavy against that upper light.","transitionFromPrevious":"The dome's contained radiance opens here into an unenclosed split — light and dark occupy separate halves rather than one surrounding the other."},{"slot":"W041","whyHere":"Two hard light beams slice through layered nested rectangles, pulling the eye from a dense scribbled left edge toward glowing ovals that read as sources rather than reflections.","transitionFromPrevious":"The two white discs of the previous work reappear here as two beams cutting through structure rather than burning within an open field."},{"slot":"W190","whyHere":"Two white-hot rectangles anchor the composition while zigzag lines spread outward in yellow and cyan; the dark upper-left cluster feels compressed against that brightness.","transitionFromPrevious":"The beams of the previous work have condensed into two fixed rectangular sources, and the surrounding marks now radiate outward from them rather than crossing them."}]},{"title":"Machines, Shells, and Scatter","introduction":"Three works where the surrounding space is structured by geometry or noise — frames, domes, and static that hold or release what is inside them.","stops":[{"slot":"W219","whyHere":"A horizontal bar with oval recesses anchors the upper field while downward triangles and surrounding zigzag lines read as noise holding the central forms in charged suspension.","transitionFromPrevious":"The two glowing rectangles of the previous work reappear here as oval recesses in a machine-like bar — the light sources have become buttons, and the surrounding scatter has become more organised."},{"slot":"W224","whyHere":"Two diagonal beams slice through a field of zigzag borders and nested rectangles; glowing spiral cores inside the arched form hold still against all that surrounding movement.","transitionFromPrevious":"The bar and triangles of the previous work give way here to diagonal beams crossing a similarly noisy field — the geometry shifts from horizontal to diagonal, and stillness moves from the bar into the spiral cores."},{"slot":"W098","whyHere":"Placed here as a contrast: the yellow field surrounding this face is the quietest surround in the exhibition, making the contained pressure of the face more legible against the calm.","transitionFromPrevious":"After two works dense with zigzag noise, the plain yellow field here reads as sudden silence — the surrounding space has been stripped back, and the face must carry the charge alone."}]}]}
